name: Hand axe
desc: A bifacially shaped stone tool of the Acheulean tradition, used for butchering, chopping and digging for over a million years.

name: Wedge
desc: A tapered tool that converts a driving force into splitting force; the working principle behind blades, axes and chisels.

name: Hafting
desc: Attaching a stone point or blade to a handle with binding or adhesive, multiplying leverage and reach.

name: Axe
desc: A hafted blade swung to fell trees and split wood; enabled forest clearance and timber building.

name: Ground stone tools
desc: Tools shaped by grinding and polishing against abrasive stone, giving durable edges for axes and adzes.

name: Hammer
desc: A hafted striking tool that delivers concentrated impact for shaping, driving and forging.

name: Spindle
desc: A weighted rod spun by hand to twist fibers into yarn, the basis of all spinning for millennia.

name: Adze
desc: A hafted blade set crosswise to the handle for smoothing and hollowing timber, used to build boats and houses.

name: Chisel
desc: A wedge-edged blade driven by a mallet to cut and shape wood, stone and later metal.

name: Bow drill
desc: A drill spun by the string of a bow, used for boring beads, teeth, wood and for starting fires.

name: Forging
desc: Shaping heated metal by hammering, the basic method of making tools and weapons for millennia.

name: Lost-wax casting
desc: Casting metal in a mould formed around a wax model that is melted out, allowing intricate detail.

name: Wheel and axle
desc: A simple machine in which a wheel fixed to a shaft multiplies torque, the basis of winches and cranks.

name: Metal casting
desc: Pouring molten metal into a mould to make complex shapes in one step.

name: Saw
desc: A toothed blade for cutting wood and stone; copper saws appear in early Egyptian woodworking.

name: Anvil
desc: A heavy metal block on which hot metal is hammered into shape.

name: Rivet
desc: A metal pin hammered over at both ends to join plates; later key to boilers, ships, bridges and aircraft.

name: Inclined plane
desc: A ramp that trades distance for force, used to raise heavy stones for Egyptian and Mesopotamian monuments.

name: File
desc: A hardened bar with cut teeth for removing metal, essential for fitting parts before machine tools.

name: Forge welding
desc: Joining iron pieces by heating them to near melting and hammering them together; the oldest welding method.

name: Crane
desc: A lifting machine using pulleys and a boom, introduced by the Greeks for building with large stone blocks.

name: Calipers
desc: Earliest known caliper, a wooden piece with a fixed and a movable jaw, found in the Greek Giglio wreck, 6th century BC.

name: Winch
desc: A drum turned by a crank to wind a rope, giving mechanical advantage for hauling and lifting.

name: Block and tackle
desc: A system of multiple pulleys that multiplies lifting force; attributed to Archimedes.

name: Archimedes' screw
desc: A helical surface inside a tube that lifts water when turned, used for irrigation and draining mines.

name: Treadwheel crane
desc: A crane powered by people walking inside a large wheel, used from Roman times through medieval cathedral building.

name: Worm drive
desc: A screw meshing with a gear to give a large speed reduction and self-locking action.

name: Cam
desc: A rotating profile that converts rotary motion into reciprocating or timed motion.

name: Trip hammer
desc: A heavy hammer raised by cams on a water-driven shaft, used in China and Europe for forging, hulling and fulling.

name: Belt drive
desc: A loop of flexible material transmitting rotation between pulleys; used on early Chinese quilling and spinning wheels.

name: Crank
desc: An arm at right angles to a shaft that converts between rotary and reciprocating motion.

name: Hand plane
desc: A blade held in a body at a fixed depth for flattening and smoothing wood; known from Roman sites.

name: Bearing
desc: A machine element that supports a rotating shaft and reduces friction; rolling bearings are known from Roman ships at Nemi.

name: Screw press
desc: A press driven by a large screw, used by Romans for olives and grapes and later for printing and coining.

name: Connecting rod
desc: A rod linking a crank to a reciprocating part such as a saw frame or piston.

name: Hierapolis sawmill
desc: A Roman water-powered stone sawmill, the earliest known machine combining a crank and connecting rod.

name: Spinning wheel
desc: A hand- or foot-driven wheel that turns a spindle by a belt, greatly speeding up yarn production.

name: Knitting
desc: Forming fabric from interlocking loops of yarn using needles; known from Egyptian socks around 1000 CE.

name: Chain drive
desc: Transmitting power through an endless chain over sprockets; used in Su Song's astronomical clock tower.

name: Flywheel
desc: A heavy wheel that stores rotational energy to smooth out uneven power input.

name: Pole lathe
desc: A lathe driven by a cord wound around the work and tensioned by a springy pole and treadle.

name: Crankshaft
desc: A shaft with offset crank throws driving or driven by several connecting rods; described by al-Jazari.

name: Camshaft
desc: A shaft carrying several cams that operate valves or hammers in sequence; described by al-Jazari.

name: Sawmill
desc: A mill using water or later steam power to saw logs into timber.

name: Spring
desc: An elastic metal device that stores mechanical energy, used in locks, clocks and later every kind of machine.

name: Brace
desc: A hand drill turned by a cranked handle, giving continuous rotation for boring holes.

name: Nut and bolt
desc: A threaded fastener pair that clamps parts and can be undone, the standard way of assembling machines.

name: Stocking frame
desc: William Lee's mechanical knitting machine, one of the first major textile machines.

name: Rolling mill
desc: Passing metal between rollers to reduce thickness and make uniform sheet and bar.

name: Vernier scale
desc: An auxiliary scale that allows readings finer than the main scale's divisions.

name: Micrometer
desc: A screw-based gauge for measuring small dimensions precisely; Maudslay's bench version set workshop standards.

name: Flying shuttle
desc: John Kay's shuttle propelled across the loom by a picker, doubling weaving speed.

name: Carding machine
desc: Machines with wire-toothed cylinders that disentangle and align fibers before spinning.

name: Spinning jenny
desc: Hargreaves's multi-spindle spinning frame that let one worker spin many threads at once.

name: Water frame
desc: Arkwright's water-powered roller spinning machine, which led to the first cotton mills.

name: Circular saw
desc: A toothed disc rotating continuously, much faster than a reciprocating saw.

name: Spinning mule
desc: Crompton's combination of jenny and water frame that spun fine, strong yarn.

name: Line shaft
desc: Overhead shafts and belts distributing power from one engine or water wheel to many factory machines.

name: Power loom
desc: Cartwright's mechanized loom, which brought weaving into factories.

name: Centrifugal governor
desc: Spinning weights that regulate engine speed automatically; an early feedback controller.

name: Cotton gin
desc: Whitney's machine that separated cotton fibers from seeds, transforming cotton supply.

name: Ball bearing
desc: A rolling bearing using hardened balls between races, patented by Philip Vaughan in 1794.

name: Hydraulic press
desc: Bramah's press using Pascal's principle to multiply force, used for forming, baling and extrusion.

name: Extrusion
desc: Forcing material through a shaped die to make long profiles; first used by Bramah for lead pipe.

name: Screw-cutting lathe
desc: A lathe with a lead screw and change gears that cuts accurate threads; Maudslay's made standard screws possible.

name: Portsmouth Block Mills
desc: Brunel and Maudslay's steam-powered machines that mass-produced pulley blocks for the Royal Navy.

name: Mass production
desc: Making large quantities of standardized products with specialized machines and divided labor.

name: Jacquard loom
desc: A loom attachment controlled by punched cards, allowing complex patterns and inspiring computing.

name: Band saw
desc: A continuous toothed steel band running over wheels, used for curved and resawing cuts.

name: Planer
desc: A machine tool that moves the workpiece under a fixed cutter to produce large flat surfaces.

name: Milling machine
desc: A machine using rotary multi-tooth cutters to shape metal; key to making interchangeable firearm parts.

name: Ring spinning
desc: Continuous spinning using a traveller on a ring, the dominant yarn method of the 20th century.

name: American system of manufacturing
desc: Production with specialized machines, jigs and gauges to make interchangeable parts, pioneered at US armories.

name: Roberts loom
desc: Richard Roberts's cast-iron power loom, the first widely successful one.

name: Sewing machine
desc: A machine that stitches cloth mechanically; Thimonnier's and later Howe's and Singer's designs mechanized garment making.

name: Shaper
desc: A machine tool with a reciprocating single-point cutter for flat surfaces and slots.

name: Die casting
desc: Forcing molten metal into reusable steel dies under pressure; first used to cast printing type.

name: Steam hammer
desc: Nasmyth's steam-driven hammer that could forge very large pieces such as ship shafts.

name: Surface plate
desc: A flat reference plate made by scraping three plates against each other, originated by Maudslay c.1800 and described by Whitworth in 1840.

name: Whitworth thread
desc: The first national screw thread standard, proposed by Joseph Whitworth.

name: Turret lathe
desc: A lathe with an indexing tool turret for repeated operations without resetting tools.

name: Hydraulic crane
desc: William Armstrong's crane driven by water pressure, widely used on docks.

name: Go/no-go gauge
desc: A fixed gauge that checks a part is within tolerance, making interchangeable manufacture practical.

name: Vernier caliper
desc: Joseph Brown's sliding caliper with a vernier scale, a standard workshop measuring tool.

name: Drop forging
desc: Forging metal between shaped dies with a falling hammer, giving uniform parts in quantity.

name: Gear hobbing
desc: Generating gear teeth with a rotating helical cutter, the main method of mass-producing gears.

name: Twist drill bit
desc: Morse's fluted twist drill that cleared its own chips, the standard metal drilling tool.

name: Pneumatic tool
desc: Tools driven by compressed air, first used for rock drilling in Alpine tunnels.

name: Servomechanism
desc: A feedback-controlled actuator; Farcot's steam steering engine gave the idea its name.

name: Injection molding
desc: Injecting molten material into a mould, patented by the Hyatt brothers and central to plastics manufacturing.

name: Automatic screw machine
desc: Spencer's cam-controlled automatic lathe that turned out screws and small parts unattended.

name: Grinding wheel
desc: A bonded abrasive wheel for cutting and finishing hard materials.

name: Grinding machine
desc: A machine that finishes parts to fine tolerances with an abrasive wheel; Brown & Sharpe's universal grinder.

name: Metal stamping
desc: Pressing sheet metal between dies to cut and form parts, used for bicycles and later car bodies.

name: Roller chain
desc: Renold's bushed roller chain, efficient power transmission for bicycles and machinery.

name: Arc welding
desc: Welding with heat from an electric arc, first done with carbon electrodes by Benardos.

name: Resistance welding
desc: Joining metal by passing current through pressed-together parts, invented by Elihu Thomson.

name: Time and motion study
desc: Measuring and analyzing work steps to set standard times and remove wasted motion.

name: Conveyor belt
desc: A moving rubber or fabric belt that carries material continuously, first used widely in mining.

name: Power tool
desc: Hand-held tools driven by motors; Fein's 1895 portable electric drill was among the first.

name: Gauge block
desc: Johansson's precision blocks that combine to give exact reference lengths.

name: Tapered roller bearing
desc: Timken's conical roller bearing that carries both radial and thrust loads.

name: Oxy-fuel welding
desc: Welding and cutting with an oxygen-acetylene flame, introduced by Fouche and Picard.

name: Shielded metal arc welding
desc: Arc welding with flux-coated electrodes, made practical by Kjellberg; still the most common manual process.

name: Powder metallurgy
desc: Making parts by pressing and sintering metal powders, first industrialized for tungsten filaments.

name: Scientific management
desc: Taylor's system of analyzing and standardizing work to raise productivity.

name: Fordism
desc: Ford's combination of moving assembly lines, standardized products and high wages.

name: Forklift
desc: A powered truck with lifting forks for moving loads in warehouses and factories.

name: Jig borer
desc: A precision machine for locating and boring holes in jigs and dies to fine tolerances.

name: Autonomation
desc: Machines that stop themselves on detecting a defect, from Toyoda's automatic loom; a pillar of Toyota's system.

name: Statistical process control
desc: Shewhart's use of control charts and statistics to monitor and stabilize manufacturing processes.

name: Pallet
desc: A flat transport platform lifted by forklifts, standardizing the handling of unit loads.

name: Chainsaw
desc: A portable saw with cutting teeth on a driven chain, transforming logging.

name: Submerged arc welding
desc: Automatic arc welding under a blanket of granular flux, used for heavy plate and pipes.

name: Blow molding
desc: Inflating a hot plastic tube inside a mould to make hollow items such as bottles.

name: TIG welding
desc: Arc welding with a non-consumable tungsten electrode under inert gas, developed for magnesium aircraft parts.

name: Electrical discharge machining
desc: Eroding metal with controlled electric sparks, able to cut very hard materials and complex shapes.

name: MIG welding
desc: Arc welding with a continuously fed wire electrode under shielding gas, fast and easy to automate.

name: Toyota Production System
desc: Toyota's system of eliminating waste through just-in-time flow and built-in quality.

name: Numerical control
desc: Automatic control of machine tools by coded instructions, first demonstrated at MIT.

name: Automated guided vehicle
desc: A driverless vehicle that follows wires or markers to move materials in factories.

name: Kanban
desc: A card-based signaling system that pulls parts through production only as needed.

name: Angle grinder
desc: A hand-held grinder with a right-angle drive for cutting and grinding metal and stone.

name: APT programming language
desc: A high-level language for generating tool paths for numerically controlled machines.

name: Plasma cutting
desc: Cutting electrically conductive metals with a jet of hot plasma.

name: Electron-beam welding
desc: Welding with a focused electron beam in vacuum, giving deep, narrow welds.

name: Machining center
desc: A CNC machine tool with an automatic tool changer that performs many operations in one setup.

name: Coordinate-measuring machine
desc: A machine that measures part geometry by probing points in three dimensions.

name: Just-in-time manufacturing
desc: Producing and delivering parts only when needed, cutting inventory and exposing problems.

name: Industrial robot
desc: A programmable multi-axis manipulator for welding, handling and assembly.

name: Unimate
desc: The first industrial robot, installed at a General Motors die-casting plant in 1961.

name: Poka-yoke
desc: Simple mistake-proofing devices that prevent or flag assembly errors.

name: Computer-aided design
desc: Using computers to create and modify engineering drawings and models, starting with Sketchpad.

name: G-code
desc: The standard language of instructions for numerically controlled machine tools.

name: Material requirements planning
desc: Computer-based planning of parts and materials needed to meet a production schedule.

name: Laser cutting
desc: Cutting material with a focused high-power laser beam, often CNC-controlled.

name: Diamond turning
desc: Ultra-precision turning with single-crystal diamond tools for optical-quality surfaces.

name: Laser beam welding
desc: Welding with a concentrated laser beam, giving fast, narrow welds suitable for automation.

name: Flexible manufacturing system
desc: Computer-controlled groups of machines and handling systems that can switch between products.

name: Programmable logic controller
desc: A ruggedized computer replacing relay panels to control factory machines, first built for GM.

name: Robot welding
desc: Automated spot and arc welding by robots, introduced on car body lines.

name: Stanford arm
desc: An all-electric, computer-controlled robot arm that shaped later robot designs.

name: Single-minute exchange of die
desc: Lean method for cutting die changeover to under ten minutes, developed at Toyota and publicized by Shigeo Shingo.

name: Water jet cutter
desc: Cutting materials with a very high-pressure jet of water, optionally with abrasive.

name: Computer-aided manufacturing
desc: Using software to generate machine tool paths directly from digital designs.

name: Humanoid robot
desc: A robot with a human-like body; WABOT-1 was first, and 2020s models target factory work.

name: Computer-integrated manufacturing
desc: Linking design, planning and production through shared computer systems.

name: Machine vision
desc: Camera-based automatic inspection and guidance of robots in production.

name: SCARA robot
desc: A selective-compliance robot arm designed for fast, precise assembly.

name: 3D printing
desc: Building objects layer by layer from digital models, first proposed by Hideo Kodama.

name: Stereolithography
desc: Curing liquid photopolymer layer by layer with ultraviolet light, patented by Chuck Hull.

name: Total quality management
desc: An organization-wide approach to continuous quality improvement.

name: Six Sigma
desc: Motorola's data-driven method for reducing process variation and defects.

name: Selective laser sintering
desc: Fusing powdered material with a laser, layer by layer, to build parts.

name: ISO 9000
desc: International standards for quality management systems.

name: Lean manufacturing
desc: The Western generalization of Toyota's methods for removing waste.

name: Fused filament fabrication
desc: 3D printing by extruding melted thermoplastic filament along a path; the most common printer type.

name: Enterprise resource planning
desc: Integrated software covering production, supply chain, finance and personnel.

name: Friction stir welding
desc: Solid-state joining by a rotating tool that stirs softened metal, invented at TWI.

name: Selective laser melting
desc: Fully melting metal powder with a laser to print dense metal parts.

name: Collaborative robot
desc: A robot designed to work safely alongside people without guarding.

name: Electron-beam melting
desc: Metal 3D printing that melts powder or wire with an electron beam in vacuum.

name: Digital twin
desc: A live digital model of a physical product or process, fed by sensor data.

name: RepRap
desc: An open-source self-replicating 3D printer that launched low-cost desktop printing.

name: Industrial internet of things
desc: Networked sensors and machines that share data for monitoring and control in industry.

name: Industry 4.0
desc: The vision of connected, data-driven smart factories, named in Germany in 2011.

name: Generative design
desc: Software that searches many design options against goals and constraints, often for additive parts.
